conventions.convention: There are N≥1 particle labels with fixed positive masses, an open configuration domain Q⊆R^(3N), and a continuous force map locally Lipschitz in state locally uniformly in time. Quantities are defined on C² curve families on intervals with nonempty interior; balance claims additionally require the equation of motion.

Angular momentum uses inertial momenta p_i=m_i x_i' and positions relative to a C¹ reference curve o; it does not replace momenta by relative velocities. The moving-origin correction is −o'×P. Internal torque is summed once over i<j.

Potential energy has the sign F_i=−∇_(x_i)U+d_i. U is C² and the residual forces have the standing force regularity. A global potential model means d≡0, including time-dependent U; it does not by itself imply energy conservation.

Potential normalization is independently time-dependent on each connected component of Q. Along a continuous motion on an interval, U→U+c_C(t) shifts E by c_C(t) and its rate by c_C'(t). Energy statements refer to a declared representative.

Frame changes use t'=t+b and x'=Rx+vt+a₀ with R∈SO(3), so the boost sign is positive. Corresponding reference curves undergo the same affine transfer, forces rotate, and the mechanical-energy law assumes the explicitly declared scalar potential transfer.

SI dimensions are retained: momentum has mass×length/time, angular momentum mass×length²/time, energy and work mass×length²/time², and power mass×length²/time³. Example numerical parameters are declared model data, not measurements.

load_bearing.statement: For a C² curve family, M=Σm_i, p_i=m_iw_i, P=Σp_i, X=M⁻¹Σm_ix_i, ρ_i=x_i−X, V=X'; J_o=Σ(x_i−o)×p_i, T_o=Σ(x_i−o)×F_i, K=½Σm_i‖w_i‖², power=Σ⟨F_i,w_i⟩, and work is the integral of power for t₀<t₁.

A potential presentation declares C² U and residual forces d_i with F_i=−∇_(x_i)U+d_i; mechanical energy along a curve family is E=K+U(t,x(t)). A global potential model has d≡0. Closed C¹ configuration-space fields have local potentials on star-shaped open subdomains, without a general global-exactness conclusion.

Along a motion with the declared potential presentation, E'=∂_tU(t,x(t))+Σ⟨d_i(t,x(t),w(t)),w_i(t)⟩. E is constant when ∂_tU≡0 and the evaluated residual forces vanish. For t₀<t₁, ΔK=U(t₀,x(t₀))−U(t₁,x(t₁))+∫[∂_tU+Σ⟨d_i,w_i⟩]dt, equivalently the same expression equals work.
For an antisymmetric external-plus-pair presentation, T_o=T_o^ext+I and J_o'=T_o^ext+I−o'×P. Evaluated central pair forces imply I≡0. If o is constant and T_o≡0, then J_o is constant.
For a motion with an antisymmetric external-plus-pair presentation, P'=σ=ΣF_i^ext and MX''=σ. If σ≡0, then P and V=M⁻¹P are constant.
Along a motion, K is C¹ with K'=power, and for every t₀<t₁ in its interval, K(t₁)−K(t₀)=∫power dt=W([t₀,t₁]). No potential or pair presentation is required.
For the stated C² curve families, P=MV, Σm_iρ_i=Σm_iρ_i'=0, and K=½M‖V‖²+½Σm_i‖ρ_i'‖². For N=2, the relative term is ½μ‖r'‖² with r=x₁−x₂ and μ=m₁m₂/M. No equation of motion is used.

At corresponding times, P̃=RP+Mv, K̃=K+⟨v,RP⟩+½M‖v‖², J̃_õ=RJ_o+(RX_o)×Mv, T̃_õ=RT_o, and power̃=power+⟨RΣ,v⟩. Work gains the integral of that extra power; under the stated motion and pair hypotheses it equals ⟨RΔP,v⟩. Under scalar potential transfer, Ẽ gains the same boost terms as K̃.

concerns.concern: Clause (f) assumes 'Let U:Q→R be C²' and concludes that U⁻¹(c) is an embedded submanifold, citing thm-a-regular-level-set-is-an-embedded-submanifold. That supplier assumes a smooth map, and def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart requires smooth slice charts. C² is insufficient for this smooth conclusion. In numerical coordinates, U(x,y,z)=z−|x|³ is C² with everywhere nonzero gradient; its zero level is a C² graph that is not a smooth embedded surface near x=0. The finite-regularity conclusion needs an appropriate supplier and terminology, or an explicit smoothness hypothesis.

The title says 'mechanical energy is available only locally', and step 3.1 concludes 'no global mechanical energy K+U of the framework's form is available for it.' This exceeds the circulation argument. def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy (a)-(b) allows residual-force presentations: U≡0 and d=F satisfy its hypotheses globally for this smooth, state-Lipschitz force and define global mechanical energy E=K. Nonexactness excludes a global force-generating potential with d≡0 and the associated static-potential conservation claim; it does not exclude globally defined mechanical energy in every allowed presentation.

The physical_scope contains the unqualified clause 'about a fixed point with vanishing external torque the angular momentum is constant.' The Statement correctly requires vanishing total torque, or central pair forces together with vanishing external torque. External torque alone does not control I: two labels with no external forces and constant opposite noncentral pair forces can have nonzero internal torque. The scope summary should explicitly carry the total-torque or centrality hypothesis into this clause.
